::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Febry 4 [1869][^2]  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS UCLA: collection 100: box 95[^1]
:::

My dear [Mrs Gatty](people/person_549.qmd)
This fairy tale strikes me as one of the very prettiest I have seen, but it is too long for the [Packet](organizations/other_52.qmd) and besides ought to be illustrated. So I send it to you, hoping you will have room for it. I am a little disturbed by Venus shining all night but I suppose Fairy land could be no where else It is a most quaint and dainty fancy that does those nursery rhymes, and I think if the word <u>rose</u> was altered she might be supposed to have got into the track of Venus ere her setting. The constellations coming to life amused me much.

Thank you for the two numbers, one of which I sent on to [Madame de Witt](people/person_423.qmd). 

What a spring it is, I am sitting at an open window, feeling like April.

Yours very sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Black-edged paper.
[^2]: Dated on the assumption that it refers to Henriette de Witt’s article 'Across the Sea’, which appeared in *[Aunt Judy’s Magazine](organizations/other_54.qmd)* (March 1869) 273-286.
